title: 2% Agarose Gel Electrophoresis
author: Alicia Grealy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdmki44w
materials: Dispose of gel waste into a biohazard bag.

steps.title: Weigh agarose powder
steps.instruction: Weigh 2.2 g agarose powder onto a weigh boat using a spatula.

steps.title: Transfer powder to flask
steps.instruction: Transfer the agarose powder into a 200 mL conical flask.

steps.title: Add TAE buffer
steps.instruction: Measure 110 mL of 1× TAE buffer with a graduated cylinder, add it to the flask, and swirl gently to mix.

steps.title: Prepare 1× TAE stock
steps.instruction: Make 2 L of 1× TAE by mixing 50 mL of 40× TAE buffer with 1950 mL Milli‑Q water; invert to mix.

steps.title: Microwave agarose (first minute)
steps.instruction: Microwave the uncovered flask for 1 min; a lid may be placed loosely to allow steam to escape. Do not microwave longer than 1 min at a time and never fill the flask more than half full.

steps.title: Handle hot flask
steps.instruction: Using oven mitts, remove the flask from the microwave, swirl gently, and keep your face away from the opening as the liquid is boiling.

steps.title: Microwave agarose (second minute)
steps.instruction: Microwave the flask for an additional 1 min, stopping early if the agarose boils excessively; swirl, examine near a light source to confirm melting, then allow to cool for 5 min.

steps.title: Set up casting tray
steps.instruction: Prepare the gel casting assembly before pouring the melt.

substeps.instruction: Place the casting tray into a rubber vice (or tape the ends with masking tape) so the ends are sealed.
Position the assembly on a flat bench and use a spirit level to ensure it is level; adjust if needed.
Insert a 20‑well comb into the casting tray.

steps.title: Add DNA stain
steps.instruction: When the flask is cool to the touch, add 5 µL SYBR Safe, swirl gently to mix, and avoid generating bubbles. Wait until the solution is warm (not boiling) before casting the gel to prevent cracking of the tray.

steps.title: Pour gel and remove bubbles
steps.instruction: Slowly pour the liquid agarose into the casting tray; pop any bubbles that form using a clean pipette tip.

steps.title: Gel solidification
steps.instruction: Allow the gel to set at room temperature for 20–30 min.

steps.title: Clean residual agarose
steps.instruction: Let residual agarose in the flask set, then scrape it into the waste bin. Fill the flask half‑full with water, microwave until the water boils, pour the water down the sink, and clean the flask with a bottle brush.

steps.title: Remove combs
steps.instruction: When the gel is fully set, gently remove the combs.

steps.title: Place gel in tank
steps.instruction: Transfer the casting tray with the solidified gel into the electrophoresis tank.

steps.title: Fill electrophoresis tank
steps.instruction: Fill the tank with 1× TAE buffer up to the fill line indicated on the tank.

steps.title: Load DNA ladder
steps.instruction: Pipette 3 µL of a 50 bp DNA ladder into the first well. If the ladder is not pre‑mixed with loading dye, add 1–2 µL loading dye before loading. Adjust volume according to the ladder’s concentration per the manufacturer’s recommendation.

steps.title: Prepare sample wells
steps.instruction: Create sample wells on a 96‑well PCR plate rack using Parafilm and load samples.

substeps.instruction: Place Parafilm across the rack and press firmly to form small wells.
For each sample, pipette 1–2 µL loading dye onto the Parafilm without piercing it.
Mix 10 µL PCR product with the loading dye by gentle pipetting up and down.
Transfer the resulting 12 µL mixture to the corresponding gel well, avoiding contact with the bottom of the well and over‑loading.

steps.title: Close tank and connect power
steps.instruction: Place the lid on the gel tank, plug the electrodes into the appropriate power slots, and ensure the positive electrode is at the base of the gel. Verify that all cords are undamaged, not a tripping hazard, and that the area is free of explosive or corrosive materials.

steps.title: Set electrophoresis parameters
steps.instruction: Turn on the power pack, set voltage to 80 V and run time to 1 h 10 min (adjustable). For small amplicons, 96 V for 30–40 min may be used; lower voltage with longer run improves fragment separation.

steps.title: Start electrophoresis run
steps.instruction: Press ‘Run’ or ‘Start’ on the power pack and observe bubbles rising from the electrodes.

steps.title: Finish run and retrieve gel
steps.instruction: When the run completes, switch off the power pack, remove the lid, and carefully lift the gel from the tank without letting it slide off the tray. Do not remove the lid until the power is off.

steps.title: Image gel under UV
steps.instruction: Place the gel on a UV transilluminator, photograph it with the attached camera following the manufacturer’s instructions, and observe UV safety protocols (training, signage, do not open transilluminator while UV is on).

steps.title: Dispose of gel and clean UV dock
steps.instruction: Discard the gel into a designated biohazard bin and clean the UV dock with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Dispose of consumables
steps.instruction: Place used pipette tips into a designated sharps container.

steps.title: Wash reusable glassware
steps.instruction: Wash used combs, beakers, flasks, and the casting tray with warm water and set them on a rack to dry.

steps.title: Seal waste
steps.instruction: Seal gloves and all chemical waste in a biohazard bag for incineration.
